info.name: Consent Manager — Data Fiduciary API
info.description:
The API a data fiduciary's systems call: raise consent requests one at a time or by the thousand, read where each
stands, verify a consent token before using personal data, and read the fiduciary's own billing and audit trail.

## Authentication

Every call except the public keys needs one of:

- **An API key** in `X-API-Key` (`cmk_…`), issued in the DF Console under *Developers → API keys* (ADR-041).
- **An OAuth 2.0 access token** from client credentials (`df-api-<your fiduciary id>`), in `Authorization: Bearer`.

Never send both.

## Signed requests (replay protection)

Each API key comes with a signing secret (`cms_…`). A signed request carries three more headers:

| Header | Value |
|---|---|
| `X-Signature-Timestamp` | The current time in Unix seconds |
| `X-Signature-Nonce` | A new random value for **every** request: 16–64 of `A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -` |
| `X-Signature` | Lower-case hex HMAC-SHA256 of the text below, keyed by the signing secret's UTF-8 bytes |

The signed text is these seven lines joined by `\n`, with no trailing newline:

```text
CM1-HMAC-SHA256
{X-Signature-Timestamp}
{X-Signature-Nonce}
{HTTP method, upper case}
{path exactly as sent, without the query}
{query string exactly as sent, without '?', or empty}
{lower-case hex SHA-256 of the exact body bytes (of no bytes when there is no body)}
```

- The timestamp must be within **±300 seconds** of the server's clock (`signature-expired` otherwise).
- A nonce is accepted **once** per key: the same signed request sent again is refused with **409
  `request-replayed`**. Retries are signed afresh with a new nonce.
- A key can **require** signatures: then every unsigned `POST`, `PUT`, `PATCH` or `DELETE` is refused
  (`signature-required`). Reads may go unsigned. A request carrying any signature header is always checked.
- Multipart uploads are signed like any other body: hash the exact bytes you send.

## Purposes (ADR-031)

A request asks consent for a **published purpose version**: what the data is for, which data, how long it is
kept, who else receives it, how long consent may last, and the notice people read, in each language. Define a
purpose, publish it, then raise requests naming `prpsCode` and `prpsVer`. A published version never changes; a
change is a new version, which the platform classifies:

- **Material** (more data, new recipients or transfers, longer retention or validity, higher sensitivity, new
  special processing): existing consents keep their old scope, and requests must name the new version.
- **Non-material** (wording, fewer categories, shorter retention): consents carry on.

Only the current version can be asked for. Asking for an older one is refused with **409
`purpose-version-superseded`**, so an integration can't silently ask for what the purpose no longer says. A
request may ask for some of the version's data categories, never others (purpose limitation).

## Errors

Errors are `application/problem+json` (RFC 9457) with a stable `title`, such as `quota-exceeded` or
`request-replayed`.

## Environments

Use the **sandbox** to integrate: the same API, its own keys and data, test contacts only (`*@sandbox.example`,
`+44 7700 900000`–`900999`), nothing delivered.
